Chapter Five: Faith Expressed Through Practical Obedience
When you think about faith, maybe you picture something you feel deep inside or ideas you hold in your mind. But the journey of truly connecting with Christ shows us something more—faith is meant to be lived out, right where we are. It’s not enough just to feel inspired or to agree with spiritual truths. Real faith? It leads us to action.
Imagine this: you’re moved during worship or while praying, and you sense Christ’s presence so strongly. You want to live differently—you really do. But then, as the day goes on, those old habits come creeping back in, and that burst of inspiration starts to fade away. Sound familiar? For most of us, it’s a pretty common story. The real challenge is figuring out how to bridge that gap between what we experience spiritually and the choices we make every day.
Here’s something to pay attention to—most people don’t realize just how much those small acts of obedience matter. It’s tempting to wait for some big moment—a huge opportunity to help or to make a difference. But honestly, faith comes alive in the ordinary choices we make. Think about the neighbor who could use a hand, the coworker who’s tough to love, or the family member who needs your patience. That’s where faith turns real.
Let me share an example. Someone once felt nudged to reach out to a person they hadn’t spoken to in a long time. But fear of being rejected held them back. It would’ve been easier to ignore that gentle prompting and just move on. Instead, remembering what practical obedience looks like, they took a risk and made contact. The response? Way more positive than expected—and that broken relationship started to heal. Just like that, it became clear how even the smallest step of obedience can open the door for Christ to work.
It’s important to remember, obedience isn’t about earning favor or proving your worth. It’s simply our way of saying “yes” to Christ’s love and His leading. Sometimes, it’s as easy as being kind; other times, it takes real courage and maybe a little sacrifice. But every single act of obedience—no matter how small—strengthens that relationship with Christ.
There’s real freedom in living this way. You’re no longer stuck worrying about making the perfect choice or being afraid to fail. Instead, you start to trust that Christ is present, guiding you as you go. Sure, you’ll make mistakes. Not every step will bring the results you hope for. But the point isn’t to be perfect—it’s faithfulness that matters most.
Over time, practical obedience starts to feel more natural. The more you practice, the easier it becomes to recognize Christ’s gentle nudges and to respond with trust. That doesn’t mean life gets easy or predictable. There will still be challenges, and sometimes the cost of obedience feels high. But what you gain is a deeper, richer sense of communion with Christ—a life that’s shaped, more and more, by His presence and purpose.
